panels.title: RPC Request Rate by Command
panels.description:
**What:** How many times each RPC command runs per second.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of command executions over 5 minutes, grouped by command name and node.
**Reading it:** Compare bars/lines across commands to see which endpoints drive load.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; dominated by whichever commands clients call most.
**Watch for:** A single command spiking far above its norm, consistent with a client hammering one endpoint.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (command, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[5m]))

panels.title: RPC Latency P95 by Command
panels.description:
**What:** The 95th-percentile response time for each RPC command.
**How it's computed:** 95th-percentile of per-command execution durations over 5 minutes, grouped by command and node.
**Reading it:** Lower is better; watch the slowest commands.
**Healthy range:** Fast lookups a few ms; heavy queries tens to hundreds of ms. Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A command whose latency climbs steadily, pointing to an expensive or degrading query path.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, command, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[5m])))

panels.title: RPC Error Rate
panels.description:
**What:** The percentage of each command's calls that finished with an error.
**How it's computed:** Error calls divided by total calls per command over 5 minutes, expressed as a percent.
**Reading it:** Green under 1%, yellow 1-5%, red above 5%.
**Healthy range:** Below 1% per command in normal operation.
**Watch for:** A command sitting red, indicating malformed input, overload, or a broken handler.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (command, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by (command, exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[5m])) * 100

panels.title: RPC Latency Heatmap
panels.description:
**What:** The full distribution of RPC response times over the window.
**How it's computed:** Counts of requests in each latency band per 5-minute window, shown as color density.
**Reading it:** A tight low band is healthy; multiple bands mean mixed fast/slow requests.
**Healthy range:** Most mass in the low-latency bands; workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A distinct high-latency cluster (bimodal behavior) that percentiles alone would hide.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

panels.title: Overall RPC Throughput
panels.description:
**What:** Two layers of the request pipeline: connections accepted by the HTTP handler versus requests parsed and dispatched.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rates of the outer request-accept layer and the inner processing layer over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** The two lines should track each other closely.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; both lines roughly equal.
**Watch for:** A gap between accept and process, meaning requests are queued or rejected before dispatch.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processSession; src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processRequest

targets.expr: sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name="rpc.http_request"}[5m]))

sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name="rpc.process"}[5m]))

panels.title: RPC Success vs Error
panels.description:
**What:** Aggregate rate of successful versus failed RPC commands across all command types.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rates of ok and errored command completions over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** Success should dominate; the error line should stay near the floor.
**Healthy range:** Error line near zero relative to success; workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A sustained error line, which warrants drilling into the per-command breakdown.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"}[5m]))

sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]))

panels.title: Top Commands by Volume
panels.description:
**What:** The ten most-called RPC commands over the recent window.
**How it's computed:** Total invocation counts per command over the last 5 minutes, ranked and capped at ten.
**Reading it:** The top bars are the hottest endpoints driving node load.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; typically led by lightweight status queries.
**Watch for:** An unexpected command dominating the ranking, consistent with automated abuse.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (command, exported_instance) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[5m])))

panels.title: WebSocket Message Rate
panels.description:
**What:** How many RPC messages arrive over WebSocket connections per second.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of processed WebSocket RPC messages over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** Non-zero only when clients use WebSocket; zero is normal for HTTP-only nodes.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; zero if no WebSocket clients.
**Watch for:** A sudden surge from a single source, consistent with a chatty or abusive subscription client.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processSession

targets.expr: sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name="rpc.ws_message"}[5m]))

panels.title: RPC Resource Cost by Command
panels.description:
**What:** RPC traffic grouped by resource-cost category rather than by command name.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of commands over 5 minutes, grouped by load/cost category.
**Reading it:** Cheap categories should dominate; costly ones should be a small slice.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; low-cost categories carry most traffic.
**Watch for:** Growth in high-cost categories such as exception or malformed requests, which point to problematic clients.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (load_type) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", load_type!=""}[5m]))

panels.title: Batch vs Single RPC Requests
panels.description:
**What:** The rate of batched RPC requests versus single-command requests.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rates of batch and single requests over 5 minutes, per node.
**Reading it:** Single requests usually dominate; batch is used by bulk clients.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; batch typically a minority.
**Watch for:** A batch rate climbing sharply, consistent with bulk automation or amplification attempts.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processRequest

targets.expr: sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="rpc.process", is_batch="true"}[5m]))

sum by (exported_instance) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{exported_instance=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="rpc.process", is_batch="false"}[5m]))
